elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: New second sentence: "Client may assign or transfer its rights under this Agreement without approval to an affiliate..." — unconditional, and the prior "financially responsible" qualifier no longer limits Client's right.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: "...or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets" without approval — all three trigger events expressly named.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: "TrueLink shall not assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of Client"; the former mutual no-approval affiliate exception is deleted, so no Vendor consent-free route survives.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: "...prior written approval of Client, which shall not be unreasonably withheld" — reasonableness standard attaches to the Vendor-side consent only.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: "...and shall never assign to a competitor of Client" — absolute bar, not curable by consent as drafted.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: "...a change of control of Client shall give TrueLink no right to terminate this Agreement"; no other clause in the cited text creates a transfer- or CoC-triggered Vendor right that would contradict this.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor carve-out runs to Client only; TrueLink's assignments (including to a successor) remain subject to Client's prior written approval.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No notice obligation appears; Client's successor assignment is simply "without approval" with no notice mechanic.
Client's affiliate assignment is a retained/expanded no-consent non-successor exception, which under the stated rule boundary defeats this element.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The only consent gate retained (Vendor assignments) is expressly "not to be unreasonably withheld"; the condition is satisfied for every assignment that still needs consent.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all six preferred elements are present in operative language (Vendor-only consent gate with reasonableness standard, absolute competitor bar, Client affiliate and M&A/asset-sale carve-outs, and express no-CoC-termination confirmation). Fallback is incomplete (no mutual successor right, no written-notice mechanic, retained consent-free affiliate exception), but only one complete level is required.

Minimality holds. Splitting the single mutual sentence into a Vendor-side and a Client-side sentence is the least intrusive way to break the symmetry the preferred position requires; deleting the mutual "financially responsible affiliate" exception is necessary because it was the Vendor's only consent-free route and the preferred affiliate element is unqualified. No survival tail, expense language, re-pricing bar, notice procedure, or other extra outside the checklist was added.

Intent preserved: the redline grants no new Vendor assignment exception (the Customer-only successor right is implemented by carve-out to Customer, not by widening Vendor's rights), the mutual restriction survives in split form, and no undefined term or dangling cross-reference is created — "affiliate", "successor" and "change of control" are used in their ordinary sense consistent with the original drafting.

Drafting note only (not a defect): consider adding "and shall not be a permitted assignee by consent either" is unnecessary, but if TrueLink pushes back on the absolute competitor bar, the offered fallback in the comment (mutual successor right on written notice, consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld) would require deleting the Client affiliate exception to be complete.
